newsitem.title: UK: BOE - personal sector liquidity may fan inflation.
newsitem.headline: BOE - personal sector liquidity may fan inflation.

text.p: Bank of England governor Howard Davies said the Bank was concerned that rapid growth of personal sector deposits -- a key component of broad money supply -- may signal a future pickup in both inflation and activity.

"We are concerned because we cannot explain adequately the growth of personal sector deposits over the last 18 months in terms of what has been happening to personal sector income, wealth and consumption and to relative interest rates," he said.
"We therefore regard the apparent overhang of personal sector liquidity as generating an upside risk to future activity and inflation," Davies told a London Business School conference.

Davies estimated the liquidity overhang at around ten billion pounds, or about two percent of total M4. He said the Bank was more worried by this then by the fact that the broad measure of money supply (M4) was growing at "around the top" of its three to nine percent monitoring range.
It has grown at a year-on-year rate of nine percent or above for the last eight months.
"And the recent strength of the corporate sector deposits could be a harbinger of future investment growth, again contributing to a pick up in activity," Davies added.
